newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Highlights of Friday's Commission briefing.
newsitem.headline: Highlights of Friday's Commission briefing.

text.p: Following are highlights of the midday briefing by the European Commission on Friday:

Spokeswoman Sarah Lambert said the Third Pan-European Transport Conference would take place in Helsinki from Monday to Wednesday. She said it would bring together 60 Transport ministers and experts from the European Union and from Eastern Europe. She said discussions would focus on the integration of transport policies, the Trans-European Networks (TEN) corridors and technological developments.

Spokesman Jean-Christophe Filori said the International Donors conference for Bosnia scheduled on Tuesday 24 in Brussels had been cancelled on the advice of International High Representative to Bosnia Carl Bildt. Filori said the conditions set at the ministerial-level meeting in Sintra (Portugal) for the conference to take place had not been fulfilled. Filori said the conference would take place when they had been met.

Spokesman Willy Helin said the Commission had adopted a proposal on an EU/U.S. positive comity agreement. In answer to a question he said both that agreement and the existing EU/U.S. cooperation agreement on competition issues specifically excluded mergers in their provisions.
The Commission released the following documents:
- IP/97/544: Commission adopts a proposal on EU/US positive comity agreement.
- IP/97/547: The Commission authorises the acquisition of joint control by Bank of America and General Electric on the Spanish company Cableuropa.
- Speech/97/143: Speech by Commissioner Franz Fischler on the CAP and Rural Development: Europe must play a winning game.
- Memo/97/62: Calendar of the Commission activities for June 23-28, 1997.
- Eurostat news release No 44/97: EU Direct Investment Flows abroad: ECU 95.4 billion in 1996.
- Eurostat - Statistics in focus - Economy and Finance No 1997-20: EU Direct Investment Flows, first results of 1996 figures.
- Helsinki Third Pan-European Transport Conference - Press Pack.
